original_question: For a finite group G, can one always choose a generating set A so that the sequence of sphere sizes S(1), S(2), S(3), ... determined by word length with respect to A is unimodal? The paper notes that computations usually show unimodality but that a general theorem is unknown, even for nonabelian finite groups.
target_in_paper: Section 2010.1.4 (Peter Hegarty): the finite-group unimodality conjecture arising from the broader phase-transition discussion, namely that every finite group admits some generating set for which the sphere-size sequence is unimodal.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right target and is already very close to the paper's actual finite-group statement. It correctly asks for existence of a generating set for each finite group, not unimodality for every generating set; it matches the paper's intended inclusion of nonabelian finite groups; and it accurately reflects the nearby computational context that non-unimodal examples can occur for particular generating sets even though computations usually show unimodality.
missing_details: A stand-alone version should say explicitly that the sequence under discussion is the cardinality sequence |S_A(1)|, |S_A(2)|, |S_A(3)|, ... rather than the sets S_A(r) themselves.
The notation S(r) is left implicit in the paper, so a self-contained question should define S_A(r), e.g. as the sphere of radius r in the word metric associated to the generating set A.
The word-length convention should be fixed explicitly, for example using the shortest expression in letters from A union A^{-1}.
The meaning of unimodal should be stated: there exists an index m such that the sphere sizes are weakly increasing up to m and weakly decreasing thereafter.
Because G is finite, the sequence eventually becomes 0; a stand-alone formulation should note that S_A(r)=empty set for all sufficiently large r.

To stay paper-faithful, the question should not be broadened to the preceding infinite-group or compact-Abelian measure-setting discussion, which is context rather than the specific finite-group conjecture.
refined_question: Does every finite group G admit a generating set A such that, if l_A(g) denotes the word length of g with respect to A and S_A(r) := {g in G : l_A(g) = r}, then the sphere-size sequence (|S_A(1)|, |S_A(2)|, |S_A(3)|, ...) is unimodal; that is, there exists m >= 1 for which |S_A(1)| <= ... <= |S_A(m)| >= |S_A(m+1)| >= ... , with |S_A(r)| = 0 for all sufficiently large r?
justification: The exact statement your draft is aiming at is the last sentence of 2010.1.4, where the paper records Hegarty's conjecture that for any finite group, not necessarily abelian, one can find a generating set making the relevant sequence unimodal. The immediately preceding lines in the same item provide the intended context: the notation S(1), S(2), ... is introduced, the discussion turns to unimodality of their sizes or measures, and the paper notes computational evidence for finite groups together with counterexamples for some generating sets. An earlier nearby remark also confirms the finite-group feature that eventually all spheres are empty. Since the paper gives this only as an informal problem-session note and does not formally define S(r), the refined version adds just the standard sphere/word-length definitions needed to make the conjecture fully stand-alone, without broadening it beyond the finite-group question actually singled out there.
